title: feat: show community model creators in the key model picker
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
The model picker used for creating keys, editing keys and app consent now makes community models easy to tell apart from official ones.

- Community models show their creator's GitHub username (`@user`) after the name
- Selected community models use the Quest Pollen green; selected official models use the pale paid amber, so both read at the same strength (the full-strength amber was overpowering next to the green)
- Adds `amber` / `green` intents and a `detail` slot to `TabButton` in `@pollinations/ui`, so Enter passes semantic props instead of its own classes; both are shown in the showcase
- Other tab buttons keep their current colours

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Selected official | strong amber | pale amber |
| Selected community | strong amber, name only | pale Quest green + `@user` |
| Unselected community | neutral | green label + `@user` |

gist.headline: Give the gardeners credit
gist.blurb: Community models get a name tag in the key and consent pickers: their creator’s GitHub handle. A little Quest Pollen green helps distinguish them from official models without making either selection shout.
gist.summary: The model picker for key creation, key editing, and app consent adds creators’ GitHub @user handles to community models and distinguishes selected community models with pale Quest Pollen green from official models with pale amber.
gist.impact: People choosing models can identify community creators at a glance, while the two selected states remain equally readable and other tab buttons keep their existing colors.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy model-picker screen with two balanced tabs: a pale amber official model and a lime-green community model labeled with a small @user handle. Polli, wearing tiny reading glasses, points out the creator credit; a code-plant and flowers bring the garden motif into the interface.
